Subject: Call: logging controls & PII redaction — CareCo discovery

Hi Emily / Adam — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align on engineering scope and legal checkpoints. Happy to jump on a follow-up if you'd prefer a quick screen share.

Key takeaways from today's call:
- Primary ask: reduce PII exposure in request/response logs and headers while preserving observability for debugging and billing.
- Trace IDs: CareCo needs unique transaction correlation but does not want full-UUIDs stored in logs long-term.
- Retention: default logs retention target is 90 days; legal asked whether 30/90/180 options are supported.
- Residency: data must remain in us-east-1 for EU-regulated customers, but CareCo asked for confirmation that processing can be limited to US-only regions.
- Evidence/Compliance: they requested a basic SOC2 artifact list and example filtering spec.

Options discussed (engineering implications):
1) Trace ID handling — three patterns: drop entirely; hash (one-way) at ingest; or truncate to first 8 bytes. Hash preserves correlation across systems but makes cross-referencing harder without raw token. Truncate keeps some uniqueness but risk of collisions.
2) Header scrubbing — configurable allowlist per route; redact values server-side with replace token (e.g., <REDACTED>) and keep header keys for routing metrics.
3) Request/response level redaction — automatic key-based redactors (json path) + opt-in full-body pseudonymization for a subset of partners.
4) Sampling & aggregation — sample raw payloads at 1% for debugging or store only aggregated metrics to lower retention costs.

Proposed acceptance criteria for pilot:
- No raw PII (email, SSN, full credit card) preserved in plaintext logs for more than 24 hours.
- Trace correlation retained for at least request-level troubleshooting via hashed trace IDs (HMAC with per-customer salt) if CareCo chooses hashed option.
- Admin console toggle for header allowlist and retention periods per environment (dev/stage/prod).

Next steps / owners (proposed):
- Engineering POC: Karthik to validate hashed-trace implementation and estimate perf hit (ACTION: karthik_iyer) — target: 2-week POC.
- Compliance/Legal: Marcus to share SOC2 artefact checklist and redact-spec draft (ACTION: marcus_lin) — ETA: 3 business days.
- CareCo decision: Emily/Adam to pick trace-id option (drop/hash/truncate) and confirm retention target (ACTION: emily.chen@careco.com) — ETA: EOD Wed.

Attachments: redaction-spec.pdf (draft) — contains suggested jsonPath patterns + header allowlist template.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Call: logging controls & PII redaction — CareCo discovery

Marcus — really helpful summary, thank you. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Retention: Our security team is comfortable with 90 days for aggregated logs, but requests/response bodies containing any PII must be purged after 7 days unless explicitly flagged for debugging.
- Trace ID: we prefer hashed trace IDs (HMAC with customer salt) so we can correlate without storing raw IDs. Important that salt rotation is supported.
- Sampling: 1% raw payload sampling is fine for now; we need a manual on/off for sampling per environment.
- Residency: yes — all processing and storage must remain in US regions for now (US-only requirement). We will scope EU residency later.

I'll review the attached redaction-spec and confirm which jsonPaths we need to redact. Can you include a short runbook for debugging when a trace is hashed? That will help our SREs.

Best,
Emily
Director, Platform Security
CareCo Health
